skill.name: env-and-assets-bootstrap
skill.description: Prepares conservative environments and asset plans for README-documented deep learning reproductions. It identifies dependency files and records dataset, checkpoint, and cache assumptions.
skill.summary: Plan reproducible research environments and asset locations before running experiments.
skill.author: lllllllama

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, conservative policy prose, or fixed shell wrapper operations. The bootstrapper performs real package installation, and SKILL.md references an instruction file outside the reviewed package boundary.

remediation.issue: The bootstrapper creates environments and installs repository dependencies when dry-run mode is not selected.
remediation.suggestion: Default to dry-run and require explicit confirmation before installation. Warn that dependency metadata and editable installs can execute untrusted code.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md directs the agent to read an instruction file outside the reviewed skill package.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the required principles inside this skill and reference an in-package path. Review and integrity-check that content with every release.

content.value_statement: Research repositories often leave environment and asset requirements incomplete. This skill builds a conservative setup plan and records unresolved dependency and asset risks.
actual_capabilities: Detects supported top-level conda, requirements, pyproject, and setup files.
Builds platform-aware setup plans for Windows, macOS, and Linux.
Creates conda, mamba, or virtual environment setup commands.
Finds checkpoint, dataset, model, cache, and download hints in README and configuration files.
Writes an asset manifest with source hints, target paths, and status values.
Supports dry-run output before environment creation or dependency installation.
limitations: It does not verify that dependencies, checkpoints, or datasets are trustworthy.
It only inspects selected top-level environment files and common configuration directories.
It does not run experiments, interpret papers, or validate reproduction results.
Asset discovery uses keyword and path patterns, so incomplete repositories may produce missing hints.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Research Repository
use_cases.description: Create an environment and asset plan before attempting a documented deep learning reproduction.

use_cases.title: Standardize Reproduction Setup
use_cases.description: Generate consistent setup notes and unresolved risk records across several research repositories.

use_cases.title: Review Student Project Requirements
use_cases.description: Identify missing dependencies, dataset locations, and checkpoint assumptions before supervised lab work begins.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Setup Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [repository path]. Create a setup plan from its README and top-level environment files without executing commands.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Required Assets
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare an asset manifest for [repository path] under [assets directory]. Record checkpoint, dataset, cache, source, path, and unresolved status.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Dry Run
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a dry-run environment plan for [repository path] on [operating system]. Prefer [manager] and use Python [version].

prompt_templates.title: Audit Cross-Platform Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [repository path] across [platforms]. Reconcile README instructions, environment metadata, asset paths, and execution risks before proposing commands.

output_examples.input: A repository with environment.yml, a declared environment name, and README checkpoint links.
output: Environment source: the documented conda file.
Assets: checkpoint links and expected local paths.

output_examples.input: A repository with requirements.txt and no documented dataset location.
output: Environment approach: an isolated virtual environment with the documented requirements.
Assets: common dataset and cache directories are marked missing.
Unresolved risk: the required dataset source needs confirmation.

output_examples.input: A repository without a supported environment specification.
output_examples.output: The plan recommends an isolated virtual environment and records the missing dependency specification as an unresolved setup risk.

best_practices: Review every proposed command and dependency source before allowing installation.
Use dry-run mode first and keep the target repository inside an isolated workspace.
Verify dataset and checkpoint sources against the repository or primary paper.
anti_patterns: Do not treat discovered URLs or filenames as proof of trustworthy assets.
Do not execute setup scripts from an untrusted repository without isolation and review.
Do not infer successful reproduction from a completed environment setup.

faq.question: Does this skill download datasets or checkpoints?
faq.answer: No. It records source hints, expected paths, and status values for later review.

faq.question: Which environment managers are supported?
faq.answer: The bootstrapper supports conda and mamba, with a Python virtual environment fallback.

faq.question: Can I preview actions without installing packages?
faq.answer: Yes. Use dry-run mode to print planned bootstrap actions without executing them.

faq.question: Which operating systems are covered?
faq.answer: The planning logic provides activation guidance for Windows, macOS, and Linux.

faq.question: Does the skill validate dependency security?
faq.answer: No. You must review package sources, build scripts, and repository trust before installation.

faq.question: Does this skill run or evaluate the experiment?
faq.answer: No. It prepares environment and asset assumptions before execution and does not assess results.
